accepted.question_text: Let N be a compact closed Riemannian manifold, isometrically embedded in R^m, and let u belong to W^{1,n}(B^n, N). If u is weakly n-harmonic, meaning that it is a critical point of the n-Dirichlet energy among range variations, must u always be continuous on B^n?

evidence.quote: Despite several results that we describe in the next section, the following problem is still open. Problem 2.2 (p = n). Are all weakly n-harmonic maps u ∈ W1,n(Bn, N ) continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let n > 2, let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, R^{n+1}) solve the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u, where J_u = ∂u/∂x_1 × ... × ∂u/∂x_n is the vector of n x n minors of Du. Must every such weak solution be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. Let n > 2. Suppose that H : R^{n+1} -> R is bounded and Lipschitz. Are all weak solutions u ∈ W1,n(Bn, R^{n+1}) of (2.5) continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B^n, R^m) satisfy the degenerate elliptic system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u, where Ω is an antisymmetric matrix-valued field in L^n(R^{m x m} ⊗ R^n). Does this antisymmetric-potential structure force u to be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.5. Let u ∈ W1,n(Bn, Rm) satisfy a system of the form (2.6) - div (|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u.
Assume that Ω = (Ω^α_ij) ∈ L^n(R^{m×m} ⊗ R^n) is antisymmetric, i.e. Ω^α_ij = -Ω^α_ji for all 1 ≤ i, j ≤ m. Is it true that u is continuous?

accepted.question_text: Let R = (R_1, ..., R_n) be the vectorial Riesz transform. Is the endpoint Lorentz-space estimate ||f||_{L^{(p,∞)}}^{p-1} <= C ||Σ_{α=1}^n R_α(|Rf|^{p-2} R_α f)||_{L^{(p',∞)}} valid?
accepted.context_brief: Endpoint Lorentz estimate for Riesz transforms

evidence.quote: A reformulation of this additional problem is the following. Problem 3.2. Let R = (R1, . . . , Rn) be the vectorial Riesz transform. Is it true or false that ||f||_{L(p,∞)}^{p-1} ≤ C ||Σ^n_{α=1} Rα(|Rf|^{p-2}Rαf)||_{L(p′,∞)} ?

accepted.question_text: Let u = (u^1, ..., u^{n+1}) ∈ W^{1,n}(Ω, R^{n+1}) be a weak solution of the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u, where H: R^{n+1} -> R is bounded and Lipschitz. If exactly k of the coordinate functions of u are known to be bounded for some k in {1, 2, ..., n}, must u be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4. Let u = (u1, u2, . . . , un+1) ∈ W1,n(Ω, R^{n+1}) be a weak solution of the H-system (2.5), where H : R^{n+1} -> R is bounded and Lipschitz. Assume that k of the coordinate functions ui are bounded, where k ∈ {1, 2, . . . , n}. Is u continuous?

accepted.question_text: For the p = n harmonic-map system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = |∇u|^{n-2} A_u(∇u, ∇u) and the H-system -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = H(u) J_u, the paper notes that the spaces of weak solutions remain closed under weak W^{1,n} limits even for approximate problems with a small perturbation in (W^{1,n})*. Can those closure results be exploited to construct counterexamples to regularity as weak limits of singular solutions to perturbed versions of these equations?
accepted.context_brief: Counterexamples via weak limits of perturbed solutions

evidence.quote: On the other hand, C. Wang [74], see also [40], and the second named author with A. Zatorska-Goldstein [66] have proved that for (2.4) and (2.5) - and for the corresponding approximate problems with a small perturbation in (W1,n)* added to the right hand side - the spaces of weak solutions are closed in the weak topology of W1,n.
We do not know whether these results could be used to construct counterexamples from sequences of singular solutions to perturbed versions of (2.4) and (2.5).

accepted.question_text: Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, let u ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n, R^{n+1}), and set b = H(u) ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n) ∩ L^∞(R^n). Determine the largest subspace V ⊂ H^1(R^n) for which the commutator [b, I] maps V to L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n) or to W^{1,1}(R^n), the commutators [b, R_α] map V to L^1(R^n), the Jacobian form du^1 ∧ ... ∧ du^n admits an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, and whether the answers change when u is assumed to solve an H-system.
accepted.context_brief: Endpoint commutator spaces for H-system data

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, and u ∈ W1,n(R^n, R^{n+1}), so that b = H(u) ∈ W1,n(R^n) ∩ L∞(R^n). (a) What is the largest subspace V ⊂ H1(R^n) such that [b, I]: V -> L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n)? What is the answer if we replace L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n) by W1,1(R^n)? Does this V contain the n × n minors of Du?

(b) What is the largest subspace V ⊂ H1(R^n) such that all commutators [b, Rα] of the multiplication by b with the Riesz transforms Rα, α = 1, . . . , n, map V -> L1(R^n)? Does V contain all the n × n minors of Du? (c) Does du1 ∧ . . . ∧ dun have an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, i.e. standard atoms that are, in addition, orthogonal to b? (d) Do the answers to the above questions change if u is not just an element of W1,n, but also a solution to an H-system?

accepted.question_text: Let u ∈ W^{1,n}(B, R^m) solve -div(|∇u|^{n-2}∇u) = Ω · |∇u|^{n-2}∇u, where Ω takes values in so(m) ⊗ R^n and belongs to the Lorentz space L^{(n,p)}. For which p in [1, n] does this guarantee that u is continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.3. Let u ∈ W1,n(B, R^m) be a solution to (2.6) for where Ω is an L(n,p)-matrix with values in so(m) ⊗ R^n. For which p ∈ [1, n] is u necessarily continuous?
